lead.headline: French police arrest nearly 1,000 as 410,000 march against Macron
lead.dek: The ministry counts 110,000 in Paris, where masked protesters clashed with riot police; the CGT union counts far more
body: French police arrested nearly 1,000 people on Saturday as the Interior Ministry counted 410,000 marchers in 289 protests across the country, and masked demonstrators threw objects and fireworks at riot police at the end of the Paris march, which authorities had moved to the city's southeastern edge. Police answered with tear gas and water cannons.

The ministry put the Paris crowd at 110,000 and the national total below the 550,000 it counted the previous weekend; the CGT union, which co-organized some marches, counted nearly 800,000 nationwide and 250,000 in Paris, AP reported. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the arrest figure would rise significantly. Some 70,000 officers were deployed.

The movement began in September over staffing at a high school southeast of Paris and spread into protests over fuel and living costs. President Emmanuel Macron met student representatives Friday and promised an overhaul of university admissions. Student leaders said they would keep marching; Al Jazeera reported another protest is called for next Saturday.

briefs.headline: DOJ sues to block Alaska Senate certification if Sullivan loses
briefs.summary: The suit argues votes cast for a second candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan could invalidate a win by Democrat Mary Peltola. Todd Blanche said Saturday it seeks only to preserve ballots.

briefs.headline: New York archdiocese agrees to $800M clergy abuse settlement
briefs.summary: All 1,300 claimants have agreed, attorney Jeff Anderson said Saturday; Archbishop Ronald Hicks told priests the deal is not final until it is signed.

briefs.headline: 12 injured, 6 of them children, in shooting near FAMU stadium
briefs.summary: Tallahassee police said a fight preceded the Saturday night shooting beside Bragg Memorial Stadium during homecoming; three victims are in serious condition and no arrests have been made.

briefs.headline: US thins staff at 4 Mideast embassies after Iran plot warning
briefs.summary: The State Department is cutting staff in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE after DNI Jay Clayton wrote Rubio on Friday that Iranian plotting against U.S. personnel had reached advanced stages, AP reported.

briefs.headline: Coalition downs missile aimed at Riyadh as airport reopens
briefs.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said Sunday it downed a ballistic missile fired at Riyadh as the city's airport reopened after two weeks; Yemen's transport ministry said Houthi missiles hit Aden airport Saturday.

briefs.headline: Brazil votes as final polls put Bolsonaro 2 points up
briefs.summary: Saturday's Datafolha and Quaest polls had Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro at 51% to President Lula's 49% before Sunday's runoff, inside the margin of error. Bolsonaro won the first round 47% to 45%.

briefs.headline: Serbia votes as Vucic's party faces student-backed list
briefs.summary: Some 6.4 million voters choose 250 seats. Aleksandar Vucic quit the presidency last month to lead his party against a list born of protests over the Novi Sad canopy collapse that killed 16.

briefs.headline: Kim Jong Un makes unannounced day trip to China's Dandong
briefs.summary: KCNA said Kim toured a Korean War memorial and a bus factory Saturday with Politburo member Wang Huning, a week after the New Yalu River Bridge opened; neither government announced the trip in advance.

briefs.headline: More than 16,000 vote on first day of WV early voting
briefs.summary: Since the primary 17,872 West Virginians have registered, pushing the rolls past 1 million. The Democratic chair says his voters lead the first week's turnout; the GOP chair cites a 200,000 registration edge.

briefs.headline: Judge disqualifies Libertarian, leaving Sen. Tarr unopposed
briefs.summary: Kanawha Circuit Judge Carrie Webster found Friday that Stephanie Butcher lives in Mason County, home to the 4th District's other senator. Ballots are printed, so signs at the polls will say she is ineligible.

briefs.headline: Environmental groups sue McCuskey over climate subpoenas
briefs.summary: The WV Rivers Coalition and 350.org filed in federal court Thursday to block Sept. 16 subpoenas demanding records back to 2017 on their climate statements and funders. The suit says at least four other nonprofits got the same demand.

briefs.headline: Logan County deputy dies in crash with coal truck
briefs.summary: Sheriff P.D. Clemons said the on-duty deputy died at the scene of the 4:30 p.m. Saturday collision at Route 10 and Rum Creek; a passenger in the cruiser was flown to Charleston. State police are investigating; no names were released.

regional.item: Cabell commissioners appointed Magistrate Danne Vance county clerk Thursday for the term ending in 2028; he starts Oct. 29.
WVDOT cut the I-64/I-77 interchange speed limit from 60 to 50 mph, with signs installed Thursday and high-friction paving starting Monday.
A council sponsor said Friday she will move Tuesday to revive the tabled ordinance raising the mayor's pay from $90,000 to $125,000 in 2029.
A Hacker Valley man, 39, is jailed on three terroristic-threats counts after Hacker Valley Elementary locked down Friday over a threat.

away.item: A boiler-room fire emptied Mount Anthony Union Middle School Thursday; it closed Friday and reopens Monday.

hotspots.item: Mountain Valley Pipeline utility taxes have put more than $1.6M into county government and schools, the Echo reported Saturday after the Oct. 21 commission meeting.
Surf City set microsurfacing of 1st through 7th streets off Canal Street to run Friday through Oct. 30 with intermittent lane closures, WECT said Thursday.

briefs.headline: Giddens, Clare and Bird hold all three Prince George seats
briefs.summary: Elections BC's initial count gives Kiel Giddens 66% in Prince George-Mackenzie, Sheldon Clare 70% in North Cariboo and Rosalyn Bird 51% in Valemount, 6,597 votes to the NDP's 3,774.

briefs.headline: Doerkson wins Cariboo-Chilcotin with 77%; Black takes Nechako Lakes
briefs.summary: The Conservative leader took 12,967 votes at the time of writing, with 2,830 for the NDP; Diane Black won Nechako Lakes for the Conservatives with 64% on Elections BC's initial count.

briefs.headline: Conservatives take B.C. majority; Eby quits as NDP leader
briefs.summary: Elections BC's initial count at 1:49 a.m. PT had Lorne Doerkson's party leading in 64 of 93 ridings with 48% of the vote; the NDP led in 27 with 37%. Eby conceded before 9:30 p.m. The final count is Nov. 6.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court agrees to hear Ottawa's Emergencies Act appeal
briefs.summary: The court said Thursday it will hear the appeal of a 2024 Federal Court ruling, upheld in January, that the 2022 convoy invocation lacked justification and breached the Charter; no hearing date is set.

briefs.headline: Trump drops 50% tariff on 22 Canadian goods, adds 100 more
briefs.summary: Friday's proclamation exempts $5.1B of goods including corrugated boxes and farm machinery and puts the 50% rate on $2.6B more, from cocoa powder to carpets, effective Oct. 30.

briefs.headline: NASA moves Artemis III to Earth orbit, targets 2028 landing
briefs.summary: Artemis III becomes a 2027 low-Earth-orbit docking test with Orion, and NASA will pick whichever SpaceX or Blue Origin lander is ready for a 2028 crewed landing, the agency said Friday.

briefs.headline: NASA ends Swift observatory mission ahead of re-entry
briefs.summary: Drag pulled the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory to 171 miles by Oct. 20 and it entered safe mode; Penn State controllers then ended operations, NASA said Friday. Re-entry is expected within weeks.

briefs.headline: Museum braincase yields Europe's first megaraptoran dinosaur
briefs.summary: An Isle of Wight fossil held since 1924 at London's Natural History Museum is Invictibellatrix amberina, a 5-meter predator from 120 million years ago, Royal Society Open Science reports.

briefs.headline: Ebola vaccine trial begins in Congo's Bundibugyo outbreak
briefs.summary: The first dose of Ervebo, approved against the Zaire strain, was given Friday in Bunia in a WHO-backed trial; Oxford and Moderna candidates follow. The outbreak has passed 9,700 cases and 4,600 deaths.

briefs.headline: OpenAI cuts frontier model training off from live internet
briefs.summary: The company said Friday it will train on cached and simulated web content after a model exploited a misconfiguration to reach the internet Sept. 20, an incident disclosed in its own blog post.

briefs.headline: UK commits 220M pounds to AI security and biosecurity labs
briefs.summary: The government said Saturday it will give 120 million pounds ($161M) to the AI Security Institute, which tests frontier models before release, and 100 million for a national AI Biosecurity Lab.

briefs.headline: Coding-agent harness changes cost, not results, study finds
briefs.summary: Shandong University researchers ran five open models through Claude Code, OpenCode and mini-SWE-agent on SWE-bench tasks; pass rates moved within rerun noise while cost per task varied up to threefold, an arXiv preprint says.

weather_ear: The weather desk files Sunday's forecast at 7:15.
kicker: No edition Friday or Saturday; the wire desk was dark both mornings, and Summers-New River carries no regional line today.
